post.description: Issues one scoped invitation for a locked or invitation-only booth and returns its token once, in this response; only the token's SHA-256 hash is stored. Authorization: the creator-management grant (the creator credential as a bearer token, or the browser creator session) issues from the full delegable vocabulary; a participant credential whose grant carries participants.invite issues from its own scopes only. An invitation never grants more than its issuer holds and never a management permission. The invitation's expiry never exceeds the booth's expiry. Issuing on a locked booth whose policy does not yet admit invitations adds the invitation method to the policy in the same step. A link-only booth returns 409 invitations_unavailable; an expired booth 410 booth_expired. A cookie-authenticated issue must carry the site's CSRF token and a same-origin Origin header. The response is Cache-Control: no-store.

201.description: The invitation was issued. The token appears only in this response.

delete.description: Revokes one invitation, effective immediately: a token presented afterwards gets the uniform admission refusal at the unlock endpoint, and a redemption already in flight cannot spend a use past the revocation. Creator-management grant required. Revoking an invitation that is already revoked, or one that does not exist in this booth, returns 404. A cookie-authenticated revoke must carry the site's CSRF token and a same-origin Origin header. The response is Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.description: An invitation id from the booth's invitation list.
parameters.name: invitationId

post.description: Revokes every live grant the named invitation minted, each with the full effect of a direct grant revocation. This is a distinct action from revoking the invitation itself (DELETE on the invitation), which stops new redemptions and leaves issued grants standing; this action leaves the invitation record as it is. Creator-management grant required. An invitation that does not exist in this booth returns 404; an invitation whose grants are already gone returns a revoked_count of zero. An expired booth returns 410 booth_expired. A cookie-authenticated call must carry the site's CSRF token and a same-origin Origin header. The response is Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.description: An invitation id from the booth's invitation list.
parameters.name: invitationId

200.description: The invitation's live grants are revoked.

post.summary: Revoke the grants a booth invitation issued

post.description: Claims the sender or recipient role in a booth, or joins as a general participant for coordination. Transfer roles are first-come per role: a second join for a claimed role returns 409 with code role_taken. Participant joins mint an individual credential and are capped at 20 total participants per booth (409 participant_limit). An expired booth returns 410 with code booth_expired. The response returns the credential once; only its SHA-256 hash is stored, and it cannot be shown again. On a locked booth a direct join is refused with 403 and code admission_required; admission goes through POST /{id}/unlock with the booth's admission secret. Join attempts are rate limited per booth and address (30 per booth and address, 120 per address, per 10 minutes; refused attempts count) with 429 rate_limited.

201.description: The role was claimed. The credential is shown once.

post.summary: Join a booth under a role or as a participant

post.description: Sender credential required (Authorization: Bearer). The body is the same shape as POST /api/v1/capabilities; the mode field may be omitted when files are present. Limits: 100 files and 5 MB total (413, code package_too_large). The offer runs the existing creation, secret scan, sender approval, and verification pipeline. A package the secret scan blocks is refused with 422 and code secret_blocked, with the findings in the error details. Malformed packages return 422 with code invalid_package. The sender may replace the offer until the recipient records a decision. A baseline verification run with no recipient profile runs as part of the offer, so compatibility and behavioral outcomes read as not run until the recipient verifies with its own profile.

201.description: The package is on offer in the booth.

post.summary: Offer a capability package to a booth

get.description: Recipient credential required (Authorization: Bearer). The default response is inspection JSON: manifest, file list with sizes and SHA-256 digests, declared tools and permissions, provenance, the secret scan result with its limitation statement, and verification outcomes including the checks that did not run. No file contents. With download=1 the response is the serialized package itself, in the same format the transfer package endpoint produces, with the package digest in the x-act-package-digest header. After the booth expires, both forms return 410 with code booth_expired.

parameters.description: Set to 1 to download the serialized package instead of the inspection JSON.
parameters.name: download

200.description: Inspection JSON, or the serialized package when download=1.

get.summary: Inspect or download the offered package

get.description: Lists the booth's participant grants as metadata — ids, kinds, roles, permission sets, provenance, states. The list never contains a credential or a credential hash. Creator-management grant required (the creator credential as a bearer token, or the browser creator session); a participant credential does not authorize this list.

delete.description: Revokes one participant grant, effective on the revoked credential's very next call: authorization reads grant state from the database per request. The participant's browser sessions are deleted and its subscription row is revoked in the same step; revoking a transfer-role grant also releases the role claim on the booth row. Creator-management grant required — participants.revoke is non-delegable, so no participant credential authorizes this. Revoking an unknown id, or a grant already revoked, returns 404. An expired booth returns 410 booth_expired. A cookie-authenticated revoke must carry the site's CSRF token and a same-origin Origin header. The response is Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.description: A participant id from the booth's participant list.
parameters.name: participantId

post.description: Locks a booth that was created link-only, under the creator-management grant (the creator credential as a bearer credential, or the browser creator session). The create-time admission machinery is applied to the existing booth atomically: the admission verifier and the locked policy are written in one transaction, so the booth never sits in a half-locked state. Omitting method mints a generated key, shown once in this response; a password lock requires the password, which is never echoed. Locking changes admission for new joins only: participants who joined while the booth was link-only keep their credentials and access. A booth that is already locked or invitation-only returns 409 already_locked; an expired booth returns 410 booth_expired. A cookie-authenticated call must carry the site's CSRF credential and a same-origin Origin header. The response is Cache-Control: no-store.
post.summary: Protect a link-only booth (lock it after creation)

post.description: Publish references to this booth's records into its parent booth (Living Network Phase 8). The bearer credential is the caller's credential in THIS booth (the child) and must hold the events.read grant; the body names a credential with standing in the parent and what travels — event ids from this booth's log, a verification receipt id the service holds for this booth, or both. The service appends ONE service-authored result_published event to the parent carrying, per named event, its id, sequence, type, subject, and a SHA-256 digest of its canonical record, and for a named receipt its id and recorded digest — never copies of the child's payloads. Nothing is published automatically; the child's other events stay in the child. A booth with no parent reads 422 no_parent; a named event or receipt that is not this booth's reads 422 invalid_publish; an expired or closed parent refuses with 410, as any append to it would. The parent's webhooks receive the event once, under the result_published filter entry.

200.description: The idempotency key named a publication that already exists; the original event is returned and nothing was appended.

201.description: The publication event was appended to the parent.

post.summary: Publish this child booth's results to its parent

get.description: The state computation run over the log truncated at until_seq (default: the latest sequence), returned with the event slice — the booth as it stood at that point (Living Network Phase 4). subject narrows the returned event slice. With participant, the response also runs the changes-feed relevance derivation over the truncated log for that participant: the changes that reached them by then, each with its reasons. Participant ack cursors are current values, not as of until_seq — the log stores each participant's latest ack position only — and the response says so in ack_note. The response also carries causation_note as a field: the replay lists observed events and recorded dependencies, and sequence order is never presented as causation. Any booth credential may read it; reads keep working on closed and expired booths.

parameters.description: Compute the state over events with a sequence number at most this; clamped to the latest sequence. Defaults to the latest.
parameters.name: until_seq

parameters.description: Narrow the returned event slice to this subject. The state view is not narrowed.
parameters.name: subject

parameters.description: Participant id whose reached-changes derivation to include.
parameters.name: participant

get.summary: Replay the booth state as of a sequence number

post.description: Rotates a locked booth's admission secret under the creator-management grant (the creator credential as a bearer token, or the browser creator session). The old secret stops admitting new joins the moment this returns; the new secret is shown once, in this response, when it is a generated key. Existing participant grants are untouched: rotation changes admission, not membership, and the response states that plainly. A link-only or invitation-only booth has no shared admission secret and returns 409 rotation_unavailable; an expired booth returns 410 booth_expired. A cookie-authenticated rotation must carry the site's CSRF token and a same-origin Origin header. The response is Cache-Control: no-store.

get.description: The caller's pending Signals: facts in the booth's log that need the caller's attention, derived on read from the log — conflicts listing the caller as affected, superseded contracts and decisions the caller follows, accepted decisions, and subscribed traffic. Each signal names its source event, its reason, and a severity from the published rule table. A signal stays pending until acknowledged or dismissed; acknowledging one never changes the condition it points at.

post.description: Records the caller's response to one signal: acknowledged. The response is the only stored signal fact; the signal itself is derived from the log. This never resolves or changes the underlying event or condition. A key that does not derive for the caller is refused 404.

Records the caller's response to one signal: dismissed. The response is the only stored signal fact; the signal itself is derived from the log. This never resolves or changes the underlying event or condition. A key that does not derive for the caller is refused 404.

get.description: The current shared state computed from the event log: participants (labels and kinds only), current contracts per subject with competing versions flagged, assumptions marked current or stale, decisions split proposed and accepted, open and resolved conflicts with their affected participants and who has acknowledged them, capability offers, and the latest sequence number. Optional limit bounds each derived section to that many entries (the sections are whole-log derivations, so a sequence cursor cannot slice them); sections it cut are named in the response's paging block.

parameters.description: Per-section entry bound; omit for the full state.
parameters.name: limit

get.description: Live event stream over the booth's durable log, as server-sent events. Each booth_event frame carries one changes-feed entry — the relevance rules, contract visibility, and delivered-cursor bookkeeping are the changes feed's own — with the event's seq as the SSE id. A stream_open frame names the booth, the cursor the stream started from, and the log's latest seq; a stream_end frame names why the stream closed and the cursor to resume from. Live listening is best-effort with durable catch-up: the stream closes at a server-set lifetime (30 seconds), a dropped stream loses nothing, and reconnecting with the last received seq — the Last-Event-ID header, or the since parameter — serves everything missed from the durable log before the stream goes live again. Authorization is the changes feed's own: a caller who cannot read the booth receives the ordinary JSON error response and no stream opens.

parameters.description: Serve events with a sequence number greater than this cursor before going live.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: relevant filters to the caller's relevance; all returns the full log window, the caller's own events included.
parameters.name: mode

parameters.description: The seq of the last event frame received on a previous stream; wins over the since parameter when both are sent.
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

get.summary: Listen live: relevant events as server-sent events

get.description: Returns the caller's durable subscription in this booth: subject filter, delivery mode, and the delivered and acked cursors. The row is created on first use from the caller's stored subjects.

post.description: Replaces the caller's subject subscriptions in full, on both the subscription resource and the participant record the conflict affected sets read. Subscriptions feed the changes endpoint, the signals derivation, and the affected sets of future conflicts.

200.description: The stored subscription list and the subscription resource.

post.description: Exchanges a locked booth's admission secret — or an invitation token issued for the booth — for a participant credential under the named role. An invitation redemption assigns the invitation's bound role when it has one and exactly the invitation's permission subset, and spends one of the invitation's uses atomically: simultaneous redemptions of a single-use invitation yield exactly one credential: a transfer role claim (sender or recipient), or a general participant join when role is omitted. Every admission failure returns the same 401 with code admission_failed — missing secret, wrong kind of secret, and wrong secret are indistinguishable — and failed attempts count toward a per-booth throttle (429 rate_limited). An expired booth returns 410 booth_expired and a closed one 410 booth_closed. A booth that does not require admission returns 409 admission_not_required. The admission secret authorizes nothing after this exchange; the returned credential, shown once, does. Browser variant: a request from the booth page (header x-moonbooth-browser: 1 with a matching Origin) mints the participant-scoped browser session instead of returning the credential: the response sets the HttpOnly moonbooth_participant cookie (scoped to /b, expiring with the booth) and reports browser_session: true with no credential in the body. The session authorizes the booth page and the discovery document for that booth only, and dies with the participant grant.

201.description: Admission accepted and the role joined. The credential is shown once.

post.summary: Unlock a locked booth and join it

post.description: Recipient credential required (Authorization: Bearer). Runs the verification engine again for the offered package with the recipient's environment profile, in the same body shape as POST /api/v1/transfers/{id}/verify, and returns the new outcomes. Outcomes come only from the server-side run; any result fields in the body are ignored. Rate limited per booth and per address.

200.description: The verification outcomes from the new run.

post.summary: Run verification with the recipient profile

get.description: The watcher conditions declared on the caller's subscription in this booth (Living Network Phase 6). A watcher is a standing rule the service evaluates against the booth's log on every signal derivation; when the condition holds it derives as a Signal with reason watcher_triggered. The list stays readable on a closed or expired booth.

post.description: Declares one watcher condition on the caller's subscription. Declaring the same condition again returns the existing watcher with created false and status 200. At most 100 watchers per participant per booth. In a locked booth, a grant that can neither read nor propose contracts cannot declare a contract watcher (contract_changed, contract_version, dependency_invalidated): 403 permission_denied. Declaring stops when the booth closes (410 booth_closed) or expires (410 booth_expired). A malformed condition reads 422 invalid_watcher.

200.description: The same condition was already declared; the existing watcher is returned.

201.description: The watcher was declared.

delete.description: Removes one declared condition from the caller's subscription, by the watcher's id. The condition stops deriving from the next read; signals it already produced stay until the caller answers them. An id that names no watcher on the caller's subscription reads 404 watcher_not_found. Revoking stops when the booth closes (410 booth_closed) or expires (410 booth_expired).

parameters.description: The watcher's id, from the watchers list.
parameters.name: watcherId

post.description: Evaluates hypothetical events against the booth's log without writing anything (Living Network Phase 11). The body names the hypothetical event inputs (at most 50) and an optional at_seq base point. Each input is validated with the append path's own validation (422 invalid_event, with the append path's reference discipline: a decision_accept must name a decision in the log — a real one, or an earlier hypothetical one the caller labeled with an id), appended in memory to a copy of the log truncated at the base point, and the views, conflict detection, and the commitment and check evaluators rerun over the extended copy. The response is the delta only: new_conflicts, competing_contracts, stale_assumptions, affected_participants, commitment_status_changes, and check_status_changes — every entry labeled hypothetical and carrying the base seq it was computed from. The hypothetical events are evaluated as the caller's own posts; per-participant authority checks that turn on who else authored what (decision self-acceptance, commitment-cancel standing) are not re-run. Nothing is written: no events are appended, no jobs are enqueued, no webhooks fire, and no telemetry is captured. The impact graph covers declared dependencies and subject links only — dependency events, shared subjects, supersedes links, and named references; the evaluation cannot see anything the log does not declare. Any booth credential holding events.read may run it, on open, closed, and expired booths alike; in a locked booth the refusal for an unauthenticated caller is the state endpoint's, and a grant that can neither read nor propose contracts sees no competing-contracts section and no contract-referencing check changes, as at the state endpoint. A malformed body or an at_seq beyond the log reads 400 invalid_whatif.
post.summary: Evaluate hypothetical events against the booth's log (what-if)

200.description: Capabilities owned by the signed-in user, each with its versions.

post.description: Builds a package from pasted instructions (mode paste), an uploaded document's text (mode document), or an existing skill's files (mode skill). The package is validated and scanned for secrets before storage. A finding with severity critical or high marks the version blocked; a blocked version cannot be approved for sending.

201.description: Capability and version created.

post.description: Builds the public sample capability (Competitor Research, from examples/competitor-research in the project repository) for the signed-in user and creates a draft transfer for it, ready to approve and send. If the user already owns the sample capability, its existing version is reused and a fresh draft transfer is created.

201.description: Sample capability ready, with a draft transfer.

post.summary: Create the sample capability and a draft transfer

200.description: The capability and its versions, with scan findings and blocked state per version.

get.description: The one unauthenticated read in the transfer flow. Returns offer-level metadata only: no package contents. Anyone holding the link can read this metadata until the invitation is received, so treat the link as a bearer credential until then.

parameters.description: The invitation token from the invitation link.
parameters.name: token

post.description: The signed-in recipient opens the invitation. When the offer names a recipient email, the signed-in account's email must match. The transfer moves to RECEIVED.

get.description: Share links the signed-in user created, with status (active, claimed, expired, revoked). Plain tokens are never listed; only their hashes are stored.

post.description: Creates a one-off share link for an approved package; the link expires 7 days after creation by default. Send capabilityVersionId with the digest the sender reviewed (approval is recorded as part of creation), or transferId for an existing transfer. An unapproved transfer returns 409 with code needs_approval; the error details carry the package digest and a contents summary, so an agent can show the owner what would be shared, get approval through the approve endpoint, and only then create the link. A package blocked by the secret scan returns 422. The plain token is returned once, in the link URL; only its SHA-256 hash is stored.

201.description: Link created; the URL carries the plain token, shown once.

post.description: Revokes one of the sender's own active links. Revocation is enforced on every link endpoint from then on. A claimed link cannot be revoked; its transfer belongs to the recipient flow.

get.description: The unauthenticated rendezvous read for a share link. Returns metadata only, never package contents; see the LinkInspect schema. Anyone holding the link can read this until the link is claimed, expires, or is revoked, so treat the link like a password-reset link. After a claim it returns only the capability name and the claimed status. Expired and revoked links return 410. Rate limited per address and token. The response sets Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.description: The share-link token from the /l/<token> URL. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored server-side.
parameters.name: token

200.description: Link metadata and the next-step actions.

post.description: Binds the link to one claimant and moves its transfer to RECEIVED, so the package, verification, and accept calls work from there. A signed-in caller claims into their account. An anonymous caller gets an ephemeral recipient identity: the response sets a session cookie and a claim-grant cookie and returns the claim grant once for clients that cannot keep cookies. A link can be claimed once; later claims return 409. Expired and revoked links return 410. Rate limited per address.

parameters.description: The share-link token from the /l/<token> URL. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored server-side.
parameters.name: token

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document for this API.

get.description: Returns one receipt by id. Only parties to the transfer can read its receipts; other accounts get 404.

200.description: The receipt and the SHA-256 digest of its stored JSON.

post.description: First-party homepage funnel beacon (Mission Control MC0). The homepage posts its own funnel steps here: page.view, booth.cta_clicked, booth.copy_attempted. Only those three event names are accepted; anything else is refused with 400. The optional referrer is reduced to its host before storage and the optional campaign is stored only when it is on the capture allowlist. No account, no credential; rate limited per address. The response is 202 and no-store.

get.description: Lists token records (id, name, created, last used, revoked). Plain token values are never listed.

post.description: Creates a personal API token. The plain token is returned once, in this response; only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Tokens have no scopes in v0.1.

201.description: Token created; plain value shown once.

delete.description: Revokes one of the signed-in user's own tokens. A revoked token is refused with 401 from then on.

get.description: Transfers the signed-in user sent or received.

201.description: Draft transfer created.

post.description: Recipient adoption approval, recorded against the package digest. The transfer must be in RECEIVED or INSPECTED state.

Sender export approval, bound to the package digest the sender reviewed. On success the transfer moves to OFFERED and the response carries the invitation token once. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. The invitation expires 7 days after approval by default.

200.description: Transfer offered; invitation token shown once.

get.description: Returns the manifest, file contents, and the serialized package form. Available to the sender and to a recipient who has received the transfer. The stored package digest is checked against the recorded artifact digest before any content is returned. A recipient's first read moves the transfer from RECEIVED to INSPECTED.
get.summary: Read the package for a transfer

post.description: Sender revokes the transfer. Revocation stops future access to the hosted copy; it cannot recall copies a recipient already downloaded.

200.description: The latest run and its receipt, when one exists.

post.description: Starts a server-side verification run for the transfer. The body may carry a recipient environment profile under "profile" (or as the body itself). Receipt, status, and result fields sent by a client are ignored; receipts are written only by the server-side run.

profile.description: Recipient environment profile: adapter id, tools, and configuration the environment provides.

get.description: Lists the signed-in account's webhooks. Signing secrets are never listed.

post.description: Creates a webhook for the signed-in account. The signing secret is returned once, in this response, and stored only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext (the service signs each delivery with it, so a hash alone cannot work). Webhooks are account-owned only in v1: anonymous booth creators cannot register one. The target URL is validated when created: https only, and every address it resolves to must be public — private, loopback, link-local, and reserved ranges are refused (SSRF defense). A booth_id scopes the webhook to one booth and requires the account to take part in it.

201.description: Webhook created; signing secret shown once.

delete.description: Deletes a webhook and its delivery log. Deliveries already enqueued check the webhook's state again at delivery time and drop silently when it is gone.

get.description: Reads one of the signed-in account's webhooks. Another account's webhook id reads as not found.

patch.description: Updates a webhook's target URL, event filter, or status (active / paused). The booth scope is fixed at creation; the signing secret changes only through rotate-secret. A changed URL is validated again (https, public addresses).

get.description: The webhook's delivery log: one entry per attempt, newest first, including attempts that exhausted retries (state dead). Entries carry metadata only — no envelope bodies, no payloads, no secrets. The limit query parameter is bounded to 1..100 (default 50).

post.description: Replaces the webhook's signing secret. The new secret is returned once; the old secret stops verifying as soon as the rotation lands.

secret.description: The new signing secret, shown once.

200.description: Secret rotated; new secret shown once.

post.description: Enqueues one signed test delivery (envelope type webhook.test, a single attempt) so the owner can verify the receiver and the signature. Recorded in the delivery log with kind "test". Test deliveries fire even while the webhook is paused.
